title: How to Link Aadhaar with PAN Online - 2-Minute Process 2026
meta_description: Link Aadhaar with PAN card online 2026. ₹1,000 penalty for late linking. Step-by-step guide on incometax.gov.in. Check linking status.

hero.one_liner: Link Aadhaar with PAN in 2 minutes online - mandatory under Section 139AA. Late linking attracts ₹1,000 penalty. Unlinked PAN becomes inoperative.

sections.heading: Why Aadhaar-PAN Linking is Mandatory
content: Under Section 139AA of the Income Tax Act, linking your Aadhaar with your PAN is mandatory for all PAN holders (except NRIs and persons above 80 years of age). This rule has been in effect since 2017 with multiple deadline extensions.

What happens if you don't link: (1) Your PAN becomes 'inoperative' - you cannot file ITR, (2) You cannot open new bank accounts or demat accounts, (3) TDS is deducted at double the normal rate (source loses deduction benefit), (4) Pending tax refunds are not credited, (5) Online transactions above ₹50,000 fail, (6) Investment account opening gets blocked.
Late linking penalty: If your PAN is unlinked and you link after the deadline, a penalty of ₹1,000 applies. This fee was introduced in 2023 and continues as of 2026.
However, the penalty is waived in some circumstances - you can appeal.

sections.heading: Who Needs to Link - Quick Check

rows.label: Must Link
rows.value: All Indian residents with both Aadhaar and PAN. Non-resident Indians (NRIs) with PAN but no Aadhaar, persons above 80 years of age without Aadhaar are exempt.

rows.label: Already Linked?
rows.value: If you filed ITR in past 3 years, likely linked. If you opened PAN after 2017 and got Aadhaar, likely linked automatically. Check status before paying ₹1,000 fee.

rows.label: NRI Exception
rows.answer: NRIs don't have Aadhaar, so exempt. If NRI gets Aadhaar later, linking becomes mandatory.

sections.heading: How to Link Aadhaar with PAN - Step by Step

steps.title: Visit incometax.gov.in → Quick Links → 'Link Aadhaar'
steps.description: Go to incometax.gov.in. Look on the left sidebar or top menu for 'Link Aadhaar' or 'Link Aadhaar-PAN'. Click it. You'll see a form asking for PAN and Aadhaar.

steps.title: Enter PAN and Aadhaar numbers
steps.description: Fill in: (1) Your 10-digit PAN (e.g., ABCDE1234F), (2) Your 12-digit Aadhaar number. Ensure PAN matches your ITR PAN exactly. Aadhaar should be the active number from your Aadhaar card.

steps.title: Check name matching
steps.description: Enter your name exactly as it appears on your Aadhaar. Even minor spelling differences (e.g., 'Rajesh Kumar' vs 'Raj Kumar') will cause failure. If names don't match, you must first correct either your Aadhaar or PAN before proceeding. See FAQs for name correction process.

steps.title: Check if you need to pay ₹1,000 fee
steps.description: If linking is overdue (past the extended deadline), the portal will ask you to pay ₹1,000 late fee. If you haven't linked yet and this is your first attempt, you may not owe the fee (depending on whether deadline has passed). Pay online via 'e-Pay Tax' if required. Wait 4-5 working days for payment to reflect before trying to link again.

steps.title: Verify with Aadhaar OTP
steps.description: Click 'Validate with Aadhaar OTP'. An OTP is sent to your Aadhaar-registered mobile number. You have 5 minutes to enter the OTP. If OTP doesn't arrive: (a) Your mobile may not be registered with Aadhaar. Update at aadhar.uidai.gov.in. (b) Wait 5 minutes and request OTP again.

steps.title: Confirm linking success
steps.description: If OTP is correct, you'll see: 'Your Aadhaar has been successfully linked with PAN' + a confirmation message. Your PAN is now active and operative. No further action needed. The linking takes effect immediately.

sections.heading: How to Check If Already Linked
content: Method 1: Online Status Check - Visit incometax.gov.in → Quick Links → 'Link Aadhaar Status'. Enter your PAN and Aadhaar.
It will show: 'Linked' (green), 'Not Linked' (red), or 'Pending' (yellow).
Method 2: SMS Check - Send SMS to 567678 or 56161 in the format: UIDPAN [12-digit Aadhaar] [10-digit PAN]. You receive a reply confirming link status within 2 minutes.
Method 3: Login and Check - If you have an incometax.gov.in account, login → My Profile → Check 'Aadhaar Number' field. If it shows your Aadhaar, you're linked.

sections.heading: Why Linking Might Fail
rows: You entered wrong PAN or PAN hasn't been registered yet
Verify PAN number. New PANs take 24 hours to activate in the system. Try again next day.
Your name on Aadhaar and PAN differ (spelling, spaces, etc.)
Update name on Aadhaar (₹50, 10-30 days) OR update name on PAN (₹107, 7-15 days). Make them match first.
DOB on Aadhaar and PAN are different
Correct the discrepancy - usually Aadhaar is accurate. Update PAN with correct DOB through NSDL.
Gender field differs between Aadhaar and PAN
Correct in Aadhaar or PAN. Rarely happens but blocks linking.
Mobile not linked with Aadhaar or network issue
Link mobile with Aadhaar at aadhar.uidai.gov.in. Takes 30 minutes. Then retry.
Your PAN and Aadhaar are already linked
You don't need to link again. You're done. If needed to confirm, check status.

sections.heading: Name Mismatch Issues - How to Fix
content: Scenario 1: 'Rajesh Kumar' on Aadhaar but 'Raj Kumar' on PAN - Names must match exactly. Options: (1) Update Aadhaar to 'Raj Kumar' (simpler, faster - ₹50, takes 10-30 days), (2) Update PAN to 'Rajesh Kumar' (₹107, takes 7-15 days).
Choose based on which document is more official. Most recommend matching Aadhaar (primary ID).
Scenario 2: 'Name Surname' on Aadhaar but 'Surname Name' on PAN - Completely reversed. This often happens with traditional name orders.
Update to match - use Aadhaar as reference.

Scenario 3: After marriage, name changed but PAN still shows maiden name - Update PAN to married name (₹107, 7-15 days via NSDL). Alternatively, keep PAN in maiden name but update Aadhaar to maiden name (keep consistency).
Document update: Visit NSDL website or authorized PAN agent.
How to update Aadhaar name: Visit myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in → 'Update Aadhaar' → Pay ₹50 → Provide proof of name change (if applicable). Takes 10-30 days.
How to update PAN name: Visit NSDL website (eservices.nsdl.com) or go through your bank's PAN update service. Requires ₹107.
Takes 7-15 days.

sections.heading: What Happens After Linking
content: Immediate benefits: (1) Your PAN becomes operative, (2) You can file ITR, (3) Bank accounts accept your PAN, (4) Online transactions above ₹50,000 work, (5) TDS is deducted at normal rates (you get deduction credit).

If you had a late linking penalty: (1) ₹1,000 fee was deducted from your account. (2) Within 30 days of successful linking, your PAN status changes from 'inoperative' to 'operative'. (3) If you can't afford the ₹1,000, you can appeal within 3 months of payment with justification (hardship, error, etc.) - amount may be waived.

Refunds and ITR filing: (1) If you had pending refunds from before linking, they're unblocked within 30-60 days of linking. Monitor your account. (2) You can now file ITR without issues. (3) Past ITRs filed while unlinked are still valid, but future ITRs require linked PAN.

sections.heading: Why Aadhaar-PAN linking is mandatory and what happens if you don't
content: The Income Tax Act (Section 139AA) makes Aadhaar-PAN linking mandatory for every PAN holder. The deadline was June 30, 2023.
If your PAN is not linked to Aadhaar by now, your PAN has become INOPERATIVE - it's essentially frozen. An inoperative PAN has severe financial consequences that affect your daily life immediately.

Consequence 1: You cannot file your Income Tax Return. The ITR filing portal rejects submissions from inoperative PANs. This means you can't claim refunds, can't carry forward losses, and can't generate ITR acknowledgment needed for loan applications, visa processing, and government tenders.
Consequence 2: TDS is deducted at 20% instead of the applicable rate. If your TDS rate is normally 10% on bank FD interest, the bank deducts 20% because your PAN is inoperative.
On Rs 1 lakh FD interest, you lose Rs 10,000 extra in TDS. This higher TDS applies to salary, professional income, rent, and all TDS-applicable transactions.

Consequence 3: You cannot open new bank accounts, demat accounts, or make financial transactions requiring PAN (property purchase above Rs 30 lakh, vehicle purchase, cash deposits above Rs 50,000). Your existing accounts continue to function, but new KYC submissions fail because the bank can't verify an inoperative PAN.

sections.heading: How to link Aadhaar with PAN - online method
content: Step 1: Visit incometax.gov.in → Quick Links → 'Link Aadhaar.' You don't need to log in - this service is available on the homepage. Click 'Link Aadhaar' button directly.
Step 2: Enter your PAN number (10-character alphanumeric - e.g., ABCDE1234F), Aadhaar number (12 digits), and name as on Aadhaar card. The name must match EXACTLY between PAN and Aadhaar.
If there's a mismatch (different spelling, missing middle name), the linking fails. Fix the name mismatch first (easier to update PAN name at tin-nsdl.com than Aadhaar name).

Step 3: Check 'I agree to validate my Aadhaar details with UIDAI.' Enter the OTP sent to your Aadhaar-registered mobile number. If your mobile isn't linked to Aadhaar, you can't complete online linking - visit an Aadhaar enrollment center to update your mobile first.

Step 4: If your PAN is already inoperative (deadline passed), you must pay a late fee of Rs 1,000 before linking. Pay at incometax.gov.in → e-Pay Tax → select 'Other Receipts (500)' → Challan 280 → pay Rs 1,000.
After payment confirmation (takes 4-7 days for NSDL to process), retry the linking. The PAN is reactivated within 30 days of successful linking + fee payment.

Step 5: After successful linking, verify at incometax.gov.in → Quick Links → 'Link Aadhaar Status.' Enter PAN and Aadhaar - the status shows 'Already linked' if successful. Your PAN is reactivated within 30 days.
In the interim, some transactions may still face issues - keep the linking confirmation screenshot for reference.

sections.heading: How to link via SMS - for those without internet
content: If you don't have internet access or are uncomfortable with the online process, link via SMS. Send an SMS from your registered mobile number to 567678 or 56161 in this format: UIDPAN [space] [12-digit Aadhaar] [space] [10-digit PAN]. Example: UIDPAN 123456789012 ABCDE1234F

The system verifies your details and sends a confirmation SMS. If the name matches between Aadhaar and PAN, linking is processed within 7 days. If there's a name mismatch, you receive an error SMS - fix the name discrepancy before retrying.

SMS linking limitation: This method doesn't work if your PAN is already inoperative (requires Rs 1,000 late fee payment first - which can only be done online or at a bank). SMS linking is best for people who haven't yet linked but whose PAN is still active (rare cases where the deadline was extended or exemptions apply).

sections.heading: Name mismatch between Aadhaar and PAN - how to fix
content: The most common linking failure reason is name mismatch. Aadhaar says 'Rajesh Kumar Singh' but PAN says 'R K Singh' or 'Rajesh Singh.' Even minor differences (extra space, missing middle name, different spelling) cause failure.
You have two options: update PAN to match Aadhaar, or update Aadhaar to match PAN.

Update PAN name (easier, recommended): Visit tin-nsdl.com → Services → PAN → 'Changes or Correction in PAN Data.' Fill the correction form, upload supporting document (Aadhaar showing correct name), and pay Rs 106 (including GST). New PAN card with corrected name arrives in 15-20 days.
After correction, retry Aadhaar-PAN linking.
Update Aadhaar name: Visit myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in → 'Update Aadhaar' → Name Update. Upload Gazette notification or marriage certificate (for name change) or passport showing correct name.
Alternatively, visit an Aadhaar enrollment center with supporting documents. Aadhaar name update takes 7-15 days.
After update, retry linking.

Date of birth mismatch: If DOB differs between Aadhaar and PAN, the linking also fails. Fix whichever is incorrect - PAN DOB correction at tin-nsdl.com (Rs 106) or Aadhaar DOB update at enrollment center.
DOB changes in Aadhaar require stronger documentation - birth certificate or 10th marksheet only.

sections.heading: Rs 1,000 late fee - how to pay and reactivate PAN
content: If your PAN became inoperative after June 30, 2023, you must pay Rs 1,000 penalty before relinking. This penalty is non-refundable and mandatory - there's no exemption or waiver regardless of the reason for delay.

How to pay: Visit incometax.gov.in → e-Pay Tax → Proceed without login → Enter PAN → Select 'Assessment Year' as the current year → Select 'Type of Payment: Other Receipts (500)' → Select 'Sub-type: Fee 234H' → Enter Rs 1,000 → Pay through net banking, debit card, or UPI. Save the challan receipt - you need the BSR code and challan serial number.

After payment: Wait 4-7 working days for the payment to reflect in the IT system. Then retry Aadhaar-PAN linking at incometax.gov.in → Link Aadhaar. The system verifies your fee payment automatically. If linking is successful, your PAN is reactivated within 30 days.
What if payment is made but linking still fails? Contact CPC helpline at 1800-103-4215 with your PAN, Aadhaar, and challan details.
The CPC manually processes cases where automatic linking fails after fee payment. This is rare but happens when there are backend data issues.
Resolution: 7-15 days after contacting CPC.

sections.heading: Who is exempt from Aadhaar-PAN linking
content: NRIs (Non-Resident Indians): NRIs who don't have Aadhaar are exempt. However, NRIs who DO have Aadhaar must link it with PAN. If you're an NRI with Indian PAN but no Aadhaar, your PAN remains active without linking.

Senior citizens aged 80+ (super senior citizens) as on the relevant date: Exempt from mandatory linking. Their PAN remains operative without Aadhaar linkage. However, this exemption is narrow - regular senior citizens (60-80) must link.

Residents of Assam, Meghalaya, and J&K: At the time the original mandate was issued, residents of these states had lower Aadhaar penetration and were exempt. Check current status - some exemptions may have been modified.
If in doubt, link anyway - there's no downside to linking even if you're technically exempt.

Non-individuals: PAN cards issued to companies, partnerships, trusts, and other non-individual entities don't require Aadhaar linking (only individual PANs need it). However, the authorized signatory of these entities needs their personal PAN linked with Aadhaar.

sections.heading: Impact on your financial life - what changes with inoperative PAN
content: Bank FDs: Interest is taxed at 20% TDS (instead of 10%). On Rs 5 lakh FD earning Rs 40,000 interest, you lose Rs 4,000 extra in TDS annually. The excess TDS can be claimed as refund - but only after you reactivate PAN and file ITR. Until then, the money is stuck with the government.

Mutual funds: You cannot make new mutual fund investments or start new SIPs with an inoperative PAN. Existing SIPs continue (as KYC was done when PAN was active), but redemptions may face issues if the AMC re-verifies PAN.
Capital gains from mutual fund sales attract 20% TDS regardless of holding period.
Property transactions: You cannot buy property above Rs 30 lakh without a valid PAN. Registration offices verify PAN at the time of registration.

Selling property with inoperative PAN attracts 20% TDS on sale consideration (instead of 1% TDS on value above Rs 50 lakh). This is a massive financial hit - Rs 20 lakh TDS on a Rs 1 crore property sale instead of Rs 50,000.

Salary: Your employer deducts TDS at 20% (highest slab without PAN) instead of your applicable slab rate. If your tax liability is 5-10% of salary, you're paying 10-15% extra TDS that's locked up until you file ITR after PAN reactivation.
Monthly impact: Rs 2,000-10,000 extra deduction depending on salary level.

sections.heading: Link NOW - every day of delay costs you money
sections.content: With an inoperative PAN, TDS on your bank interest, salary, and investments is deducted at 20% instead of the applicable rate. Every month you delay linking, you're overpaying Rs 500-5,000 in TDS that gets locked with the government. Link at incometax.gov.in in 5 minutes. Pay the Rs 1,000 late fee if applicable. Reactivation takes 30 days. The Rs 1,000 fee pays for itself within 1-2 months through TDS savings.

sections.heading: Check linking status - you might already be linked
sections.content: Many people linked Aadhaar-PAN years ago and forgot. Before panicking, check at incometax.gov.in → Quick Links → 'Link Aadhaar Status.' Enter PAN and Aadhaar number. If it shows 'Your PAN is already linked to the given Aadhaar,' you're fine - no action needed. This 30-second check saves you from unnecessary worry and the Rs 1,000 fee.

sections.text: An inoperative PAN costs you real money every month - 20% TDS on bank interest instead of 10%, 20% TDS on salary instead of your slab rate, and blocked access to property transactions, mutual funds, and new bank accounts. The fix takes 5 minutes online + Rs 1,000 late fee. That Rs 1,000 pays for itself in the first month through TDS savings. Don't let paperwork laziness drain your bank account.

sections.heading: Aadhaar-PAN linking for NRIs returning to India
content: If you're an NRI returning to India permanently, your PAN may or may not be linked to Aadhaar depending on when you left and whether you obtained Aadhaar before leaving. If you have both Aadhaar and PAN but they're not linked, the same linking process applies - visit incometax.gov.in, pay Rs 1,000 if past deadline, and link online.
If you're an NRI without Aadhaar: You were exempt from linking while abroad. Upon returning and becoming a resident, enroll for Aadhaar at your nearest enrollment center (takes 15-20 minutes).
Once Aadhaar is issued (7-15 days), link with PAN immediately. Your PAN remains active during the transition - the exemption covers the gap.

Critical for NRIs: Update your residential status with your bank from NRO/NRE to resident savings account before linking. Banks may flag discrepancies if you link Aadhaar (showing Indian address) while your bank account still shows NRI status. Update bank first, then complete Aadhaar-PAN linking.

sections.heading: Future of Aadhaar-PAN - towards unified financial identity
content: The government's long-term vision is a unified financial identity where Aadhaar, PAN, and bank account form a single verified identity ecosystem. Every financial transaction - salary, investment, property, insurance - is tracked through this linked identity.
The PAN-Aadhaar linkage is the foundation of this system.

Upcoming developments: PAN 2.0 (upgraded PAN with QR code and enhanced security features) is being rolled out. The new PAN will be automatically linked with Aadhaar at issuance - eliminating the manual linking requirement for new PAN applicants.
Existing PAN holders must still complete manual linking.

What this means for you: Linking Aadhaar-PAN is not just a compliance requirement - it's integrating you into India's digital financial infrastructure. A linked PAN enables instant ITR processing (refunds in 15 days vs months), pre-filled ITR (AIS automatically populates your income data), and seamless financial transactions across banks, mutual funds, insurance, and real estate.
The inconvenience of linking once saves you hours of paperwork every year for the rest of your financial life.

For businesses and professionals: If you're a freelancer, contractor, or small business owner, an inoperative PAN means higher TDS on every professional payment you receive (20% vs 10%), inability to file GST returns (GST registration requires active PAN), and blocked access to government tenders and contracts (active PAN is mandatory for vendor registration). The business impact of not linking is far greater than the Rs 1,000 fee.

faqs.question: I'm getting an error 'OTP not received' when trying to link. What should I do?
faqs.answer: This means your mobile number is not registered with Aadhaar. Go to myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in → 'Update Aadhaar' → select mobile update → enter your current mobile → OTP sent to that mobile → verify → saved. Takes 30 minutes. After Aadhaar mobile is updated, try Aadhaar-PAN linking again.

faqs.question: I paid ₹1,000 late fee but linking still failed (name mismatch). Am I refunded?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. The ₹1,000 fee is processed separately from the linking. If linking fails due to name mismatch, you must correct the name first, then try linking again. The ₹1,000 you paid is held but won't be refunded immediately. Once you fix the name and successfully link, the fee is adjusted against your tax account. If you believe the fee was wrongly deducted, file an appeal within 3 months with supporting documents.

faqs.question: My PAN was issued recently (2 months ago) but linking says 'PAN not found'. Why?
faqs.answer: New PANs take 24-48 hours to appear in all government databases. Wait 2-3 days and try again. If it still doesn't work after a week, contact NSDL or visit an authorized PAN agent to confirm your PAN is active in the system.

faqs.question: I'm an NRI without Aadhaar. Do I still need to link?
faqs.answer: No, NRIs without Aadhaar are exempt from the linking requirement. However, if you get Aadhaar later (by moving back to India or applying from abroad), you must link. If you're an NRI with Aadhaar and PAN, linking is recommended for smoother tax compliance, though not strictly mandatory by current rules.

faqs.question: My Aadhaar is with one mobile, PAN is linked to a different mobile. Will linking work?
faqs.answer: Yes, it will work. The linking process uses your Aadhaar-registered mobile to send OTP. As long as your Aadhaar-registered mobile receives the OTP, linking succeeds. The mobile linked to PAN doesn't matter for this process.

faqs.question: After linking, can I unlink my Aadhaar from PAN?
faqs.answer: No, unlinking is not possible. Once linked, it remains linked permanently under current rules. You cannot have a linked-then-unlinked PAN. This is by design - the linking is meant to be permanent for tax compliance.

faqs.question: I have 3 PANs (duplicate). Do I need to link all 3 with Aadhaar?
faqs.answer: You should have only 1 PAN. If you have multiple PANs, consolidate them: (1) Contact NSDL to deactivate duplicate PANs, (2) Keep one active PAN, (3) Link the active PAN with Aadhaar. Multiple PANs cause compliance issues and can trigger IT department notices.

faqs.question: Linking shows success but portal still says 'inoperative'. When does it become operative?
faqs.answer: After successful linking, your PAN status changes to 'operative' within a few hours to 1 day. Refresh the page or check next day. If still showing inoperative after 24 hours, contact IT helpline or email grievance@incometax.gov.in with screenshot of successful linking confirmation.

faqs.question: How to check if Aadhaar is linked with PAN?
faqs.answer: Visit incometax.gov.in → Quick Links → 'Link Aadhaar Status.' Enter your PAN and Aadhaar number. The portal shows: 'Your PAN is already linked' (no action needed), or 'PAN not linked with Aadhaar' (link immediately). Takes 30 seconds. No login required.

faqs.question: What is the Aadhaar-PAN linking fee?
faqs.answer: If linked before June 30, 2023: Rs 0 (free). If linking after June 30, 2023: Rs 1,000 mandatory late fee. Pay at incometax.gov.in → e-Pay Tax → Other Receipts (500) → Fee 234H → Rs 1,000. No exemption or waiver available - the fee is flat Rs 1,000 regardless of delay duration.

faqs.question: My PAN is inoperative - how to reactivate?
faqs.answer: Step 1: Pay Rs 1,000 late fee at incometax.gov.in → e-Pay Tax. Step 2: Wait 4-7 days for payment processing. Step 3: Link Aadhaar-PAN at incometax.gov.in → Link Aadhaar. Step 4: PAN is reactivated within 30 days of successful linking. During the 30-day reactivation period, some transactions may still face issues.

faqs.question: What if my name doesn't match between Aadhaar and PAN?
faqs.answer: Linking fails if names don't match exactly. Fix option 1: Update PAN name at tin-nsdl.com → Correction (Rs 106, 15-20 days). Fix option 2: Update Aadhaar name at myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in (free, 7-15 days). Updating PAN is easier and faster. After name correction, retry linking. Even small differences (extra space, middle name missing) cause failure.

disclaimer: Information is based on Income Tax Department procedures and Section 139AA as of March 2026. Deadlines, penalties, and procedures may change. Always verify current information from incometax.gov.in.
